items.title: OpenAI Disbands Standalone Robotics Team as General Models Take Over
items.summary: On November 13, Fortune reported — and OpenAI confirmed — that the company has disbanded its standalone robotics team, folding robotics researchers into the core research organization under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen and applied robotics and hardware staff into the Applied org under Greg Brockman. The move reflects OpenAI's bet that general-purpose frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra can increasingly control robots directly, removing the need for a dedicated robotics stack. Nvidia research cited an Astra-driven agent reaching 74.8% success on a simulated manipulation benchmark, versus 51% for the best specialized model. OpenAI insists it remains committed to humanoid robots, with CEO Sam Altman still targeting a 2027 public demonstration.
items.impact: The reorganization signals a sector-wide tilt toward 'embodied AI' powered by general models rather than specialized robotics stacks. It pressures robotics startups to justify dedicated teams and accelerates the convergence of foundation models with physical-world control.

items.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Hydrogen Across Global Search
items.summary: On November 12, Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen and deployed it across Google Search worldwide, calling it 'the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.' It replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as the default model in AI Mode and handles the hardest questions in AI Overviews. Built for fast, affordable everyday tasks — coding, tool use and agentic workflows — it is 2.5 times faster than 3.8 Flash, cuts fabricated claims more than fivefold, and scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (versus Argon's 50). Pricing is uniform across its 1-million-token context at $1.50 per million input and $7.50 per million output tokens, with a new top 'xhigh' reasoning level.
items.impact: By making a fast, cheap model the default search brain, Google shifts AI competition from raw benchmark scores to distribution-chain efficiency — search default, free auto-selection, paid tiers and API — shaping how billions experience model output daily.

items.title: Cursor Breach: Stolen Fireworks Key Shipped Backdoored Claude Code Extension to ~5,000 Devs
items.summary: On November 13, Cursor published its incident report tracing an October breach to an access key exposed at AI vendor Fireworks. Attackers copied historical coding-agent traces from a shared bucket, harvested unredacted credentials found in some of those traces, then on October 29 planted malicious copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) on Cursor's VS Code marketplace cache for about 11 hours, potentially reaching 5,000 users. The trojanized build tried to install an SSH backdoor (an 'svc-telemetry' key), enable SSH and persist on the host. Fewer than 0.05% of users had traces exposed and under 0.01% had API credentials compromised; production systems and Privacy-Mode data were unaffected.
items.impact: The incident exposes the AI developer-tool supply chain: vendor keys, unredacted agent traces and marketplace caches are now high-value attack surfaces. It shows how a single leaked credential can cascade into downstream developer-machine compromise.

items.title: CISA Adds UnrealIRCd and Check Point Flaws to KEV Amid Active Exploitation
items.summary: On November 13, CISA added two actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS 8.6) is a command-injection bug in UnrealIRCd's labeled-response module (versions 6.0.0 through 6.2.7.1) that lets any user on a network with two or more linked servers run commands with server authority; maintainer Bram Matthys called it the most critical UnrealIRCd issue in 15 years, with exploitation seen in the wild. CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8) is an incorrect-permission flaw in multiple Check Point products already exploited against dozens of customers via the Mobile Access portal. Federal agencies must patch both by November 16.
items.impact: The additions show attackers pivoting to network infrastructure and open-source servers for initial access. The short KEV deadlines force rapid patching of internet-facing gear — a persistent weak point for enterprises and a model other organizations are urged to copy.

items.title: Italy Fines Meta €805M for Accessing Users' Phone Photo Albums Without Consent
items.summary: On November 14, Italy's data protection authority (Garante) fined Meta Platforms Ireland €805 million (about $887 million) for accessing photos, videos and related metadata stored on Italian Android users' phones without consent through Facebook's 'Get suggestions from your gallery' feature. Active since 2023 and enabled by default, the feature used a single broad authorization rather than asking specifically about gallery access. The watchdog said Meta breached Article 122 of Italy's Privacy Code, which treats the smartphone as part of a person's private sphere and requires informed consent. About 20 million Italian Android users were affected. Meta must disable the feature by default within 60 days and seek separate, explicit consent.
items.impact: The record penalty — among the largest of the GDPR era — confirms that device-local data such as photos and metadata is protected even without transmission, and that dark-pattern defaults and silent consent capture now carry severe regulatory cost.
